Hello,

I maintain gDRplots, submitted on 4 August (BiocContributions issue #128).
Two of the three check platforms have been failing since submission, and I
think the cause is on the infrastructure side rather than in my package, so
I'd like to ask about it here.

In a single r-universe run, the runners resolve Bioconductor dependencies
from two different branches:

  linux-release-x86_64    bioconductor.posit.co/packages/devel
gDRtestData 1.11.7   OK
  macos-release-arm64     bioconductor.posit.co/packages/3.23
 gDRtestData 1.10.0   ERROR
  windows-release-x86_64  bioconductor.posit.co/packages/3.23
 gDRtestData 1.10.0   ERROR

My examples use a directory that was added to gDRtestData during the
current devel cycle, so system.file() finds it on Linux and returns "" on
macOS and Windows. That single difference is the only ERROR left on either
platform.

Is this intentional? It doesn't look specific to gDRplots ? any submission
depending on something added to a Bioconductor package during the current
cycle would fail on exactly those two platforms and pass on the third.

And a related question I genuinely don't know the answer to: is a clean
build on all platforms a precondition for a reviewer being assigned, or can
review start in parallel? My submission has been in pre-review for four
weeks and I'd like to know whether I'm waiting on this or on something else.

I do have a local workaround ? guarding the affected examples so they skip
when the data isn't installed ? but I'd rather not push it if the runners
are meant to resolve devel, since it would just hide the difference.

Thanks,
Arek Gladki

There is a slight misconception on what release and devel mean in this scenario.  They are not referring to release and devel of Bioconductor, they are referring to the release or devel version of R.  In this current cycle Bioconductor devel is still using  R-release for testing not R-devel (in prep for the new release next year).

I'm looking at your comment on the issue as well,  you reference posit repositories for bioconductor packages but those are not utilized and I'm curious as to why or how you came to that conclusion?   The Bioconductor r-universe repositories are what are being utilized for dependencies and from the detailed looks of the run, it is pulling dependencies from the correct devel r-universe of Bioconductor.

Also,  if your package is needing the higher version of gdrtestdata then that should be changed in your description file as you are also still referencing 1.6.0 version of the package.

It does seem strange that I cannot find gDRtestData in the list of installed packages during the run log; and I'm not finding it in the current Bioconductor universes.   We will follow up on this to find out why and perhaps that will clear the issue.

As far as reviewer assignment: It is an automatic system, so it waits for a clean build for the reviewer to be assigned. There is a way to override it, but let's see if we can get it resolved first by making sure the gDRtestData is available in the universe.  (I would still recommend upping the version needed in the description as that does appear to be inaccurate then) . If that does not help once its available,  we can override and go ahead with assignment while we all investigate the issue.

Cheers,


Lori Kern

Bioconductor Core Team

Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center

Department of Biostatistics & Bioinformatics

Elm & Carlton Streets

Buffalo, New York 14263

Hi Lori,

Thank you ? that resolves two of my questions and lets me correct a third
that was my own imprecision. I went back to the job logs and to the
r-universe configuration, and I think I can now point at the exact line
that produces the difference.

First, my correction. You are right that the software repository is the
Bioconductor r-universe. Every job in the run uses BioCsoft =
https://bioc.r-universe.dev. The URLs I quoted were BioCann and BioCexp ?
the annotation and experiment-data repositories, which r-universe itself
points at bioconductor.posit.co. I should have named the repositories
instead of just pasting URLs; that was misleading, sorry.

Second, on release and devel referring to R rather than Bioconductor. That
matches the job names, but I don't believe it explains this case, because
jobs running the same R end up on different Bioconductor branches. From run
33407606944:

  job                     R                  BioCexp   gDRtestData   result
  R-release for Linux     4.6.1              devel     1.11.7        OK
  R-devel   for Linux     R-devel r90452     devel     1.11.7        OK
  R-release for Windows   4.6.1              3.23      1.10.0        ERROR
  R-devel   for Windows   R-devel r90452     3.23      1.10.0        ERROR
  R-release for MacOS     4.6.1              3.23      1.10.0        ERROR
  R-oldrel  for Windows   4.5.3              3.22      1.8.0         ERROR
  R-oldrel  for MacOS     4.5.3              3.22      1.8.0         ERROR

Verbatim from the two R-release jobs, both on R 4.6.1:

  R-release for Linux

https://github.com/r-universe/biocstaging/actions/runs/33407606944/job/99540810756
      $BioCsoft
      [1] "https://bioc.r-universe.dev/bin/linux/resolute-x86_64/4.6"
      $BioCexp
      [1] "https://bioconductor.posit.co/packages/devel/data/experiment"
      trying URL
'.../packages/devel/data/experiment/src/contrib/gDRtestData_1.11.7.tar.gz'

  R-release for Windows

https://github.com/r-universe/biocstaging/actions/runs/33407606944/job/99540811117
      $BioCsoft
      [1] "https://bioc.r-universe.dev"
      $BioCexp
      [1] "https://bioconductor.posit.co/packages/3.23/data/experiment"
      trying URL
'.../packages/3.23/data/experiment/src/contrib/gDRtestData_1.10.0.tar.gz'

The R-devel Windows job (
https://github.com/r-universe/biocstaging/actions/runs/33407606944/job/99540811162)
prints the same 3.23 URLs while running "R Under development (unstable)
(2026-08-27 r90452)". Since config.yaml currently has release_version 3.23
and devel_version 3.24, those jobs are installing experiment-data packages
from the release branch, and the R version is not what decides it.

Third, where that comes from. There are two Rprofiles and they disagree:

https://github.com/r-universe-org/actions/blob/v12/Rprofile (line 1:
"currently used on Win and Mac but NOT Linux") branches on UNIVERSE_NAME.
For 'bioc' it hardcodes devel; for anything else, lines 41-42:

      bioc_anno <- sprintf("
https://bioconductor.posit.co/packages/%s/data/annotation",

 utils:::.BioC_version_associated_with_R_version())
      bioc_exp  <- sprintf("
https://bioconductor.posit.co/packages/%s/data/experiment",

 utils:::.BioC_version_associated_with_R_version())

https://github.com/r-universe-org/base-image/blob/master/Rprofile (Linux)
has the same branch structure, but its final else hardcodes devel:

      BioCann = "
https://bioconductor.posit.co/packages/devel/data/annotation"
      BioCexp = "
https://bioconductor.posit.co/packages/devel/data/experiment"

Our universe is biocstaging ? the logs print $universe = "
https://biocstaging.r-universe.dev" ? so it takes the final else in both
files: devel on Linux, R-version-derived release on Windows and macOS.

So the request to whoever maintains this: could biocstaging be treated like
bioc in r-universe-org/actions/Rprofile, so that the Windows and macOS data
repositories point at devel as they already do on Linux? As far as I can
tell it is a one-line condition. It is not specific to my package: any
submission depending on an ExperimentData or annotation package that
changed during the current devel cycle will fail on exactly those platforms
and pass on Linux, and the failure looks like a package bug rather than a
repository difference.

Fourth, on gDRtestData not appearing in the universes ? I think that is
expected and there may be nothing to find.
https://bioc.r-universe.dev/api/ls lists 2425 packages and they are all
software packages; airway, curatedTCGAData and org.Hs.eg.db are absent as
well, and gDRtestData is ExperimentData (biocViews: ExperimentData,
TechnologyData). That is exactly why BioCexp decides the outcome here ?
there is no universe copy to fall back on. (There is also a
bioconductor.r-universe.dev, distinct from bioc.r-universe.dev, which
contains only BiocManager; if that is where you looked, everything would be
missing from it.)

And you are right that the DESCRIPTION entry is stale. inst/depmap_data/
was added in gDRtestData 1.11.2, so (>= 1.6.0) does not describe what the
examples actually need. I would rather settle the repository question
before changing it, since which constraint is the correct one depends on
which branch the checks resolve.

Understood on reviewer assignment being automatic ? I would rather not ask
for an override yet. I have the examples guarded locally so they skip when
the data is absent, which would make the builds green immediately, but that
would also stop them running on Windows and macOS for the rest of the cycle
and hide the repository difference. If the Rprofile condition can be
changed, I would prefer to adjust the DESCRIPTION entry, rebuild, and let
the examples actually run.

Thanks again for digging into this,
Arek Gladki

Dear Bioconductor team,

I am the maintainer of CEMiTool. CEMiTool 1.37.0 (commit dffeb39) is
currently failing on the nebbiolo2 builder while creating the vignette
CEMiTool.Rmd.

The reported error is:

Error: processing vignette 'CEMiTool.Rmd' failed with diagnostics:
pandoc version 2.8 or higher is required and was not found
(see the help page ?rmarkdown::pandoc_available).

I was able to reproduce the failure locally using the same relevant
versions reported by the Bioconductor build environment.
Environment

Package: CEMiTool 1.37.0
Commit: dffeb39
R: 4.6.1
rmarkdown: 2.32
Pandoc: 2.7.3

The nebbiolo2 build information reports Pandoc 2.7.3, while the installed
rmarkdown version is 2.32.
Local reproduction

I used the Bioconductor Docker development image:

bioconductor/bioconductor_docker:devel

and installed rmarkdown 2.32 from the same repository used by the
Bioconductor environment:

https://p3m.dev/cran/__linux__/noble/latest/src/contrib

I then used Pandoc 2.7.3 and confirmed:

packageVersion("rmarkdown")# [1] "2.32"
rmarkdown::pandoc_version()# [1] "2.7.3"
rmarkdown::pandoc_available(version = "2.8")# [1] FALSE

Running:

R CMD build --keep-empty-dirs --no-resave-data --md5 .

produces:

* creating vignettes ... ERROR
--- re-building 'CEMiTool.Rmd' using rmarkdown
Error: processing vignette 'CEMiTool.Rmd' failed with diagnostics:
pandoc version 2.8 or higher is required and was not found
(see the help page ?rmarkdown::pandoc_available).
--- failed re-building 'CEMiTool.Rmd'

SUMMARY: processing the following file failed:
  'CEMiTool.Rmd'

Error: Vignette re-building failed.
Execution halted

Comparison

Using the same CEMiTool commit with the current Bioconductor Docker
environment, which has:

rmarkdown 2.31
Pandoc 3.10.2

the package builds successfully:

* creating vignettes ... OK
* building 'CEMiTool_1.37.0.tar.gz'

I also ran:

R CMD check --no-manual CEMiTool_1.37.0.tar.gz

which completed with:

Status: 1 NOTE

and no ERRORs or WARNINGs. The NOTE consists of standard R static-analysis
messages regarding visible bindings/global functions.
Conclusion

"The failure appears to be reproducible when rmarkdown 2.32 is used with
Pandoc 2.7.3. Could you please confirm whether this is expected for the
current nebbiolo2 build environment, and whether the builder can be updated
to Pandoc >= 2.8?

Since rmarkdown 2.32 requires Pandoc >= 2.8 for the vignette processing in
question, could the nebbiolo2 builder be updated to use Pandoc >= 2.8 (or
otherwise avoid this incompatible combination)?

Thank you.
